title: Fish and Leek Pie
subtitle: Haddock and soft leeks in a white sauce under a shortcrust lid
excerpt: Chunks of haddock and buttery leeks in a thick white sauce, baked in a shortcrust pastry case. A British supper with clean flavours.
sourceNotes: British fish pie tradition adapted as a pastry-case pie rather than the more common mashed potato topping.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the white sauce and poach the fish a day ahead. Assemble and bake the next day.

content.text: Fish breaks apart easily so handle the chunks gently when folding them into the sauce. The leeks carry a lot of water; cook them until they are dry or the sauce will thin out. Do not salt until the end because the fish brings its own seasoning.

items.prepNote: two thirds for the base, one third for the lid
white and pale green parts, sliced into rounds

content.text: Melt half the butter in the frying pan over a low heat. Add the leeks and cook for 12 minutes until very soft. Tip onto a plate.
Melt the remaining butter in the saucepan over a medium heat. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Add the milk gradually, stirring constantly, until smooth and thick. Stir in the cream and mustard. Simmer for 3 minutes.
Remove from the heat. Gently fold in the leeks, fish chunks and lemon juice. Season with black pepper. Leave to cool.
Heat the oven to 200C. Roll out two thirds of the pastry and line the pie dish. Chill for 20 minutes.
Spoon the cooled filling into the case. Roll the remaining pastry into a lid. Brush the rim with egg, press on the lid and crimp. Brush the top with egg and cut two slits.
Bake for 35 minutes until the pastry is deep gold. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

items.cause: The leeks released water or the sauce was too thin before adding the fish.
items.fix: Cook the leeks until all visible liquid has evaporated. Make the white sauce thick enough to coat a spoon before adding the fish.

items.symptom: The fish is in tiny fragments.
items.cause: The chunks were stirred in too roughly.
items.fix: Fold the fish in gently with a large spoon. Two or three careful turns is enough.

items.cause: The dish was placed on a cold shelf.
items.fix: Preheat a baking tray and bake the pie on it to get heat straight to the base.
